core_relation.sentence: A historical fact qualifies as a 'minimal fact' for resurrection belief when it is both highly evidenced (by multiple, early, eyewitness-attested data) AND held by a vast majority of qualified scholars; the evidential criterion is the dominant and sufficient condition, with scholarly consensus as a secondary confirmation.
core_relation.quote: So, if I have fewer names backing it up, I'll take that in instances where they strongly support multiple eyewitness early etc. [S095] ... That's by far the more important of the two. Way more. [S159/S160]

product_test.quote: if a fact is 51% evidence or higher that's good enough for me to believe it [S003] ... I do not have a certain threshold that they have to have to meet. [S020] ... criterion one on its own, that it being highly evidenced, that alone is sufficient for a rational belief. [S159]
product_test.reason: Habermas explicitly treats evidence as a graded threshold rather than a multiplicative product. Criterion one alone suffices for rational belief (S159); criterion two (scholarly consensus) is secondary and not strictly required. He refuses to give a numeric cutoff (S020), indicating a threshold/graduated model rather than zero-collapse multiplication.

slots.plays_role: External negentropy influx — the incoming stream of historical data and non-evangelical scholarly testimony that sustains the argument from outside the apologist's own community.
slots.quote: I think if I have non-evangelical saying those things, that that interests me [S081]

slots.plays_role: Alignment — the criterion of scholarly consensus aligns the individual's belief with the reference community of qualified scholars.
slots.quote: the vast majority of qualified scholars concur with it being a fact [S003]

slots.plays_role: Signal fidelity — the reliability of the New Testament text and the transmission of testimony through ancient sources; whether the historical signal survives.
slots.quote: the New Testament text is reliable [S021]

slots.plays_role: Effective entropy — the noise of scholarly disagreement, minority dissent, and the 'low blows' of partisan dismissal that lower the coherence of the argument.
slots.quote: critics are going to say, 'I despise 16, 18, and probably 20.' [S036]

slots.plays_role: Temporal integration — the earliness of the creedal testimony (within months of the crucifixion) accumulates evidential weight over time.
slots.quote: if it's a spring event, and you say months, it's very possible you have that proclamation in more than one place within within the remaining eight to nine months of the year. [S074]

slots.plays_role: Compression — the 'minimal facts' method itself: compressing a vast body of evidence into a small set of highly-compressed, widely-accepted claims.
slots.quote: with the minimal facts there are two criteria for something to qualify [S003]

slots.plays_role: Phase transition — the threshold at which evidence becomes sufficient for rational belief; a qualitative shift from 'probable' to 'believable'.
slots.quote: criterion one on its own, that it being highly evidenced, that alone is sufficient for a rational belief [S159]

slots.plays_role: Superposition — the unresolved state of individual historical facts before the criteria are applied; the 'open possibility' of each datum prior to evaluation.
slots.quote: 20 different evidences as critically applied using the criteria [S035]

slots.plays_role: Non-local correlation — the correlation between independent sources (Tacitus, Suetonius, Herodotus, Lüdemann, Dunn) that are no longer independent when they converge on the same fact.
slots.quote: Look at Herodotus. Look at Tacitus. Look at Suetonius before you say they don't do that stuff. [S109-S111]

slots.plays_role: Integration — the historian/apologist as the local integrator who applies the criteria and synthesizes the evidence into a rational belief.
slots.quote: I measure by do I have a fair number of multiple attestation? [S043]

one_line: Habermas's minimal-facts method is a threshold model of historical evidence where multiple attestation, earliness, and eyewitness testimony (K, T, E) integrate into rational belief, with scholarly consensus (M) as a secondary alignment factor — an analogy proposal, not a derivation.
breaks: The paper treats scholarly consensus (slot M) as optional/secondary, whereas in the master equation every factor is required for the product to hold.
Habermas explicitly refuses a numeric threshold (S020), which conflicts with the multiplicative zero-collapse model where any zero factor collapses the whole.
The 'highly evidenced' criterion is itself a threshold concept, not a multiplicative factor — the paper's logic is threshold-based, not product-based.
extra_factors: The distinction between 'they saw' and 'they thought they saw' (S066) introduces a phenomenological qualifier with no direct slot in the master equation.
The 'low blows' / ad hominem concern (S089) is a social-epistemic factor not captured by any slot.
